entries.originalText: The kingdom of God is within you,(1) saith the Lord.
entries.modernizedText: The kingdom of God is within you,(1) says the Lord.

entries.originalText: Turn thee with all thine heart to the Lord and forsake this miserable world, and thou shalt find rest unto thy soul.
entries.modernizedText: Turn to the Lord with all your heart and forsake this miserable world, and you will find rest for your soul.

entries.originalText: Learn to despise outward things and to give thyself to things inward, and thou shalt see the kingdom of God come within thee.
entries.modernizedText: Learn to despise outward things and give yourself to inward things, and you will see the kingdom of God come within you.

entries.originalText: For the kingdom of God is peace and joy in the Holy Ghost, and it is not given to the wicked.
entries.modernizedText: For the kingdom of God is peace and joy in the Holy Ghost, and it is not given to the wicked.

entries.originalText: Christ will come to thee, and show thee His consolation, if thou prepare a worthy mansion for Him within thee.
entries.modernizedText: Christ will come to you and show you His consolation if you prepare a worthy dwelling for Him within you.

entries.originalText: All His glory and beauty is from within, and there it pleaseth Him to dwell.
entries.modernizedText: All His glory and beauty is from within, and there He is pleased to dwell.

entries.originalText: He often visiteth the inward man and holdeth with him sweet discourse, giving him soothing consolation, much peace, friendship exceeding wonderful.
entries.modernizedText: He often visits the inward person and holds sweet conversation with him, giving him soothing consolation, much peace, and exceedingly wonderful friendship.

entries.originalText: Go to, faithful soul, prepare thy heart for this bridegroom that he may vouchsafe to come to thee and dwell within thee, for so He saith, if any man loveth me he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him and make our abode with him.(2) Give, therefore, place to Christ and refuse entrance to all others.
entries.modernizedText: Come, faithful soul, prepare your heart for this bridegroom, that He may graciously come to you and dwell within you, for He says, if anyone loves me he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him.(2) Therefore, make room for Christ and refuse entrance to all others.

entries.originalText: When thou hast Christ, thou art rich, and hast sufficient.
entries.modernizedText: When you have Christ, you are rich and have enough.

entries.originalText: He shall be thy provider and faithful watchman in all things, so that thou hast no need to trust in men, for men soon change and swiftly pass away, but Christ remaineth for ever and standeth by us firmly even to the end.
entries.modernizedText: He will be your provider and faithful watchman in all things, so that you have no need to trust in people, for people soon change and swiftly pass away, but Christ remains forever and stands firmly by us even to the end.

entries.originalText: There is no great trust to be placed in a frail and mortal man, even though he be useful and dear to us, neither should much sorrow arise within us if sometimes he oppose and contradict us.
entries.modernizedText: No great trust should be placed in a frail and mortal person, even though he is useful and dear to us, nor should much sorrow arise within us if he sometimes opposes and contradicts us.

entries.originalText: They who are on thy side to-day, may to-morrow be against thee, and often are they turned round like the wind.
entries.modernizedText: Those who are on your side today may be against you tomorrow, and often they turn like the wind.

entries.originalText: Put thy whole trust in God and let Him be thy fear and thy love, He will answer for thee Himself, and will do for thee what is best.
entries.modernizedText: Put your whole trust in God and let Him be your fear and your love. He will answer for you Himself and will do for you what is best.

entries.originalText: Here hast thou no continuing city,(3) and wheresoever thou art, thou art a stranger and a pilgrim, and thou shalt never have rest unless thou art closely united to Christ within thee.
entries.modernizedText: Here you have no continuing city,(3) and wherever you are, you are a stranger and a pilgrim, and you will never have rest unless you are closely united to Christ within you.

entries.originalText: Why dost thou cast thine eyes hither and thither, since this is not the place of thy rest?
entries.modernizedText: Why do you cast your eyes here and there, since this is not the place of your rest?

entries.originalText: In heaven ought thy habitation to be, and all earthly things should be looked upon as it were in the passing by.
entries.modernizedText: Your dwelling ought to be in heaven, and all earthly things should be looked upon as if in passing.

entries.originalText: All things pass away and thou equally with them.
entries.modernizedText: All things pass away, and you equally with them.

entries.originalText: Look that thou cleave not to them lest thou be taken with them and perish.
entries.modernizedText: Take care not to cling to them, lest you be taken with them and perish.

entries.originalText: Let thy contemplation be on the Most High, and let thy supplication be directed unto Christ without ceasing.
entries.modernizedText: Let your contemplation be on the Most High, and let your supplication be directed to Christ without ceasing.

entries.originalText: If thou canst not behold high and heavenly things, rest thou in the passion of Christ and dwell willingly in His sacred wounds.
entries.modernizedText: If you cannot behold high and heavenly things, rest in the passion of Christ and dwell willingly in His sacred wounds.

entries.originalText: For if thou devoutly fly to the wounds of Jesus, and the precious marks of the nails and the spear, thou shalt find great comfort in tribulation, nor will the slights of men trouble thee much, and thou wilt easily bear their unkind words.
entries.modernizedText: For if you devoutly flee to the wounds of Jesus and the precious marks of the nails and the spear, you will find great comfort in tribulation, nor will the slights of others trouble you much, and you will easily bear their unkind words.

entries.originalText: Christ also, when He was in the world, was despised and rejected of men, and in His greatest necessity was left by His acquaintance and friends to bear these reproaches.
entries.modernizedText: Christ also, when He was in the world, was despised and rejected by people, and in His greatest need was left by His acquaintances and friends to bear these reproaches.

entries.originalText: Christ was willing to suffer and be despised, and darest thou complain of any?
entries.modernizedText: Christ was willing to suffer and be despised, and do you dare complain of anyone?

entries.originalText: Christ had adversaries and gainsayers, and dost thou wish to have all men thy friends and benefactors?
entries.modernizedText: Christ had adversaries and those who spoke against Him, and do you wish to have everyone as your friends and benefactors?

entries.originalText: Whence shall thy patience attain her crown if no adversity befall thee?
entries.modernizedText: How will your patience attain its crown if no adversity befalls you?

entries.originalText: If thou art unwilling to suffer any adversity, how shalt thou be the friend of Christ?
entries.modernizedText: If you are unwilling to suffer any adversity, how will you be the friend of Christ?

entries.originalText: Sustain thyself with Christ and for Christ if thou wilt reign with Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Sustain yourself with Christ and for Christ if you want to reign with Christ.

entries.originalText: If thou hadst once entered into the mind of Jesus, and hadst tasted yea even a little of his tender love, then wouldst thou care nought for thine own convenience or inconvenience, but wouldst rather rejoice at trouble brought upon thee, because the love of Jesus maketh a man to despise himself.
entries.modernizedText: If you had once entered into the mind of Jesus and tasted even a little of His tender love, then you would care nothing for your own convenience or inconvenience, but would rather rejoice at trouble brought upon you, because the love of Jesus makes a person despise himself.

entries.originalText: He who loveth Jesus, and is inwardly true and free from inordinate affections, is able to turn himself readily unto God, and to rise above himself in spirit, and to enjoy fruitful peace.
entries.modernizedText: The person who loves Jesus and is inwardly true and free from excessive affections is able to turn readily to God, rise above himself in spirit, and enjoy fruitful peace.

entries.originalText: He who knoweth things as they are and not as they are said or seem to be, he truly is wise, and is taught of God more than of men.
entries.modernizedText: The person who knows things as they are and not as they are said or seem to be is truly wise and is taught by God more than by people.

entries.originalText: He who knoweth how to walk from within, and to set little value upon outward things, requireth not places nor waiteth for seasons, for holding his intercourse with God.
entries.modernizedText: The person who knows how to walk from within and set little value on outward things requires no particular places and waits for no particular seasons to hold communion with God.

entries.originalText: The inward man quickly recollecteth himself, because he is never entirely given up to outward things.
entries.modernizedText: The inward person quickly recollects himself, because he is never entirely given up to outward things.

entries.originalText: No outward labour and no necessary occupations stand in his way, but as events fall out, so doth he fit himself to them.
entries.modernizedText: No outward labor and no necessary occupations stand in his way, but he adapts himself to events as they happen.

entries.originalText: He who is rightly disposed and ordered within careth not for the strange and perverse conduct of men.
entries.modernizedText: The person who is rightly disposed and ordered within does not concern himself with the strange and perverse conduct of others.

entries.originalText: A man is hindered and distracted in so far as he is moved by outward things.
entries.modernizedText: A person is hindered and distracted to the extent that he is moved by outward things.

entries.originalText: If it were well with thee, and thou wert purified from evil, all things would work together for thy good and profiting.
entries.modernizedText: If it were well with you and you were purified from evil, all things would work together for your good and benefit.

entries.originalText: For this cause do many things displease thee and often trouble thee, that thou art not yet perfectly dead to thyself nor separated from all earthly things.
entries.modernizedText: For this reason many things displease you and often trouble you: you are not yet perfectly dead to yourself or separated from all earthly things.

entries.originalText: Nothing so defileth and entangleth the heart of man as impure love towards created things.
entries.modernizedText: Nothing so defiles and entangles the human heart as impure love toward created things.

entries.originalText: If thou rejectest outward comfort thou wilt be able to contemplate heavenly things and frequently to be joyful inwardly.
entries.modernizedText: If you reject outward comfort, you will be able to contemplate heavenly things and frequently be joyful inwardly.
